headline: Built a self-learning YouTube AI on AWS Aurora, barely surviving the weekend
summary: A developer built a self-learning YouTube growth AI on AWS Aurora Serverless PostgreSQL with pgvector, designed to get smarter with every user query by analyzing real-world performance data.
details: Eight months ago, the developer had no coding experience. Now, they've shipped a self-learning vector database application on AWS for a major international hackathon. This project, Virantics, aims to revolutionize YouTube growth by moving beyond generic AI tools.

The core of Virantics is a three-layer memory system, powered by AWS Aurora Serverless PostgreSQL and its pgvector extension. Instead of guessing trends, it stores the top 30% of real YouTube winners as vector embeddings, continuously learning from user queries.

The frontend was rapidly built using Vercel's v0 and Next.js, achieving a sleek, dark dashboard design. Secure backend integration was managed through AWS OIDC Federation with Vercel IAM roles, avoiding hardcoded secrets.

The biggest challenge was architecting the pgvector implementation to perform semantic similarity searches against proven patterns. A critical bug caused 30-second API timeouts due to sequential database scans. Fixing the query and rebuilding the index dramatically reduced latency to milliseconds.

The system includes an Idea Brainstormer, a Title Engine generating variations with psychological triggers, and a Thumbnail Analyzer. The developer also focused on robust SEO and metadata for discoverability, a lesson learned from previous projects.
